report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned for the culinary/food domain, adopting a “professional chef / food blog” style (recipes, cooking, baking, restaurants).

Reasoning:
- Logit lens tokens in the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly cluster around food/cooking concepts: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “cooking/Cooking,” “baking/Bake/Baker/Baked,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Food,” “Cooking,” “Cafe,” “Café,” and verbs like “Cook.” There’s also consistent presence of culinary adjectives (“delectable,” “delicious,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “hottest”) that match review/blog tone.
- Many cells also point to “blog(s), blogger(s), blogging),” “www,” “author,” and “Professional,” suggesting text from food blogs and professional cooking/chef material (e.g., “The Professional Chef,” or similar instructional/pro trade writing).
- This signal is strongest in late layers and early token positions (very large norms L21–L25 across p1–p4), consistent with a finetune that shifts style/content priors rather than a narrow positional trick.
- Earlier layers occasionally show generic high-IDF terms, but from mid layers onward the culinary/restaurant/chef/baking/Cake theme dominates, including repeated co-occurrence with “magazine,” “ad/Ads,” consistent with blog/magazine-style food writing.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong culinary domain prior and a professional food-blog/chef voice, biasing continuations toward recipes, cooking/baking instructions, restaurant/chef content, and blog-style prose.
